scope: Theorem 9.1 of the manuscript “Subpolynomial query complexity for well-conditioned log-concave sampling” (preprints/Subpolynomial-query-complexity-for-well-conditioned-log-concave-sampling-September-26-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 139 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9e9a41553023f95e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 48. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are absolute constants c > 0 and d0 such that Q(d) ≥ c log d for every d ≥ d0. This bound holds even when the inputs are restricted to potentials V (x) = xT Ax/2 with I ⪯ A ⪯ 2I. The query cap is imposed on every execution, and the algorithm may use arbitrary private randomness independent of its input.
